rules.unitsPerCarton: Quantity: {units, number} units is over {receiver}’s limit of {max, number} per carton. Pack {max, number} or fewer in each carton.
rules.cartonSize: Dimensions: {side, select, width {Width} height {Height} other {Length}} is {size, number} cm. {receiver} allows up to {shape, select, cube {{lengthCm, number} cm ({lengthIn, number} in) on each side} other {{lengthCm, number} × {widthCm, number} × {heightCm, number} cm ({lengthIn, number} × {widthIn, number} × {heightIn, number} in)}}{exception, select, oneUnit {, unless the carton holds a single unit} other {}}.
rules.cartonWeight: Weight: {weight, number} kg is over {receiver}’s limit of {maxKg, number} kg ({maxLb, number} lb){exception, select, oneUnit {, unless the carton holds a single unit} other {}}. Pack fewer units in each carton.
rules.oneSku: Products: this carton holds more than one SKU, and {receiver} takes one SKU per carton. Pack each SKU in its own cartons.
rules.packingGroups: Products: {receiver} can’t take {product} and {other} in one carton. Amazon handles them differently, for example for dangerous goods, prep or labels, and may send them to different warehouses. Move one of them to another carton.
rules.samePacking: {difference, select, units {Quantity: {sku}’s other cartons hold {units, number} units each.} other {Dimensions: {sku}’s other cartons are {length, number} × {width, number} × {height, number} cm at {weight, number} kg.}} {receiver} needs every carton of a SKU to match in units, size and weight. Match them, or ship this carton in another shipment.
rules.incompletePacks: Quantity: {sku} is sold in packs of {pack, number}. Enter a multiple of {pack, number}.
rules.missingAsin: Products: {sku} has no ASIN, which {receiver} needs to receive it. The buyer adds it on the purchase order.
rules.missingFnsku: Products: {sku} has no FNSKU, which {receiver} needs to label it. The buyer adds it on the purchase order.
rules.duplicateCarton: Carton ID: {carton} is already used by another carton. Give each carton its own ID.
rules.repeatedProduct: Products: {sku} is listed more than once in this carton. List it once, with all its units.
rules.mixedNetworks: Products: this carton mixes FBA and AWD products. Pack each network’s products in separate cartons.
rules.unknownProduct: Products: this carton holds a product that isn’t on the purchase order. Remove it from the carton.
rules.overQuantity: Quantity: the cartons hold {packed, number} units of {sku}, but the purchase order has {remaining, number} left. Remove {extra, plural, one {# unit} other {# units}}.
rules.unknownChange: Invoice changes: one change is for a product that isn’t on the purchase order, or repeats another change. Remove it.

pallets.onPallets: {count, number} of {total, plural, one {# carton} other {# cartons}} on pallets

pallets.name: Pallet {pallet}
pallets.noCartons: No cartons on this pallet yet
pallets.enterDimensions: Enter the pallet’s length, width and height.
pallets.enterWeight: Enter the pallet’s gross weight, with the pallet itself.

rules.palletFootprint: Dimensions: the load is {length, number} × {width, number} cm, over the edges of {receiver}’s {lengthCm, number} × {widthCm, number} cm ({lengthIn, number} × {widthIn, number} in) pallet. Keep the cartons within the pallet.
rules.palletHeight: Height: {height, number} cm is over {receiver}’s limit of {maxCm, number} cm ({maxIn, number} in), including the pallet. Spread the cartons over more pallets.
rules.stackableHeight: Height: {height, number} cm is too tall for a stackable {receiver} pallet, which may be up to {maxCm, number} cm ({maxIn, number} in). Set Stacking to Not stackable, or lower the load.
rules.palletWeight: Weight: {weight, number} kg is over {receiver}’s limit of {maxKg, number} kg ({maxLb, number} lb), including the pallet. Spread the cartons over more pallets.
rules.emptyPallet: Cartons: this pallet has no cartons yet. Choose its cartons, or delete the pallet.
rules.palletMixedNetworks: Cartons: this pallet mixes FBA and AWD cartons. Put each network’s cartons on separate pallets.
rules.duplicatePallet: Pallets: two pallets are numbered {pallet}. Re-import them with unique numbers.
rules.unknownPalletCarton: Cartons: {carton} isn’t a carton in this shipment. Remove it from this pallet.
rules.palletCartonTwice: Cartons: {carton} is already on another pallet. Remove it from this pallet or the other.
rules.noPallets: Pallets: these cartons ship on pallets, and there are none yet. Add a pallet, or uncheck Packed on pallets.
rules.cartonsOffPallets: Cartons: {count, plural, one {# carton isn’t on a pallet: {cartons}. Choose a pallet for it, or add a pallet.} other {# cartons aren’t on a pallet: {cartons}. Choose a pallet for each, or add a pallet.}}

palletCartons.title: Choose cartons for {pallet}
palletCartons.contentEach: {sku}, {count, plural, one {# unit} other {# units}} each

cartonImport.title: Import cartons
cartonImport.templateHint: Use the template to enter carton contents, quantities, dimensions, and weight.
cartonImport.formats: XLSX or CSV, up to 10 MB
cartonImport.failed: Couldn’t import cartons. No changes were made.

errors.empty: The file has no carton rows.
errors.worksheet: The file needs a worksheet named Cartons.
errors.unreadable: Couldn’t read this file. Use an XLSX or CSV file from the template.
errors.number: Enter a valid positive number in {value}.
errors.sku: Supplier SKU {value} and product details must match exactly one product in this shipment.
errors.cartonId: Enter a carton ID of 1–60 characters.
errors.measurements: Rows for this carton must have the same carton count, dimensions, and weight.
errors.duplicateProduct: This carton lists {value} more than once.
errors.limit: A shipment can contain up to 1,000 cartons.

columns.cartonId: Your reference for a kind of carton, not an Amazon label number: a letter for each kind, numbered from 1, such as A1, B1, C1. Repeat it on each row of a carton that holds more than one product.
columns.cartonCount: How many identical cartons of this kind. A1 with a count of 3 becomes A1, A2 and A3. IDs the shipment already has are skipped.
columns.supplierSku: Prefilled from the order. Keep it as it is, and ask the buyer to correct a missing or wrong product.
columns.quantity: Packs of this product in each carton. For a 2-pack, 10 means 20 units.
columns.weight: The packed carton’s weight in kilograms.
columns.product: Prefilled from the order. Keep it as it is.
columns.variant: Prefilled from the order. Keep it as it is.
columns.unitsPerPack: Prefilled from the order: the units in one pack. Keep it as it is.

notes.rows: Use one row per product in a carton. To pack a product in more kinds of carton, copy its row. Leave the rows you don’t use blank. The Example sheet shows the template filled in for this shipment.
notes.sameCarton: Rows with the same Carton ID are one carton: give them the same count, dimensions and weight. Identical cartons hold the same products and quantities.
notes.format: Fill in the white cells and keep the grey ones. Keep the English headers and the Cartons sheet name. Upload the XLSX file, or export the Cartons sheet as CSV.

palletImport.title: Import pallets
palletImport.failed: Couldn’t import pallets. No changes were made.

errors.empty: The file has no pallet rows.
errors.worksheet: The file needs a worksheet named Pallets.
errors.palletId: Enter a pallet ID of 1–60 characters.
errors.duplicatePallet: Pallet {pallet} is also on row {other}. Use one row per pallet.
errors.cartons: Enter the cartons on this pallet, such as A1–A6, B1.
errors.unknownCarton: {count, plural, one {Carton {cartons} isn’t in this shipment.} other {Cartons {cartons} aren’t in this shipment.}}
errors.cartonTwice: {count, plural, one {Carton {cartons} is also on Pallet {pallet}.} other {Cartons {cartons} are also on Pallet {pallet}.}} Put each carton on one pallet.

clashes.replace: {count, plural, one {These pallets clash with the pallet already on this shipment.} other {These pallets clash with the # pallets already on this shipment.}} Choose Replace pallets to use only the file’s pallets.
clashes.palletExists: There’s already a Pallet {pallet}. Give this one another ID.
clashes.cartonsOnPallet: {count, plural, one {Carton {cartons} is already on Pallet {pallet}.} other {Cartons {cartons} are already on Pallet {pallet}.}}

columns.palletId: Your reference for the pallet, such as 1, 2, 3. Use each ID once.
columns.length: The loaded pallet’s length in centimetres.
columns.width: The loaded pallet’s width in centimetres.
columns.height: The loaded pallet’s height in centimetres, from the floor to the top of the cartons.
columns.weight: The gross weight in kilograms: the pallet with its cartons.
columns.stacking: Stackable if another pallet can go on top, otherwise Not stackable. Choose from the list.
columns.cartonIds: The cartons on the pallet, by their IDs on the packing list. Join a run with a dash and separate the rest with commas. Put each carton on one pallet.

notes.rows: Use one row per pallet. The Example sheet shows the template filled in for this shipment.
notes.format: Keep the English headers, the Stacking values and the Pallets sheet name. Upload the XLSX file, or export the Pallets sheet as CSV.
